facts.raw_span: 2 progressively enlarging, painless nodular lesions on the forehead and right cheek
initially observed as erythematous nodules 3 months prior
lesions gradually increased in size with subsequent central ulceration and blackish crusting
No fever, pain, or discharge from the lesions was noted
history of kidney transplant in 2004 causing immunocompromised status
Two distinct lesions measuring 2 × 2 cm each were identified over the glabella and right cheek
lesions were firm with central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting
Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
Extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
Computed tomography of chest and abdomen showed no involvement of internal organs
Polymerase chain reaction analysis of tissue specimen was performed

support_spans: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
Extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
concepts.why: The presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos and extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages supports the diagnosis of Cryptococcosis.

support_spans: Dermoscopy showed arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment
contradict_spans: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
concepts.why: The dermoscopy findings of arborizing telangiectasias, central ulceration with crusting, and peripheral pigment are consistent with Basal cell carcinoma, but the presence of intracellular yeasts suggests an alternative diagnosis.

support_spans: lesions were firm with central ulceration with hemorrhagic crusting
contradict_spans: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
concepts.why: The presence of firm lesions with central ulceration and hemorrhagic crusting is consistent with Squamous cell carcinoma, but the presence of intracellular yeasts suggests an alternative diagnosis.

support_spans: Extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
contradict_spans: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
concepts.why: The presence of an extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages is consistent with Cutaneous histoplasmosis, but the presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos suggests an alternative diagnosis.

support_spans: Extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages
contradict_spans: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos were identified
concepts.why: The presence of an extensive dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages is consistent with Blastomycosis, but the presence of intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos suggests an alternative diagnosis.
The patient's immunocompromised status due to a history of kidney transplant increases the risk of developing cutaneous sporotrichosis.
The absence of internal organ involvement as shown by computed tomography of chest and abdomen, along with the presence of skin lesions, is consistent with mycetoma.

rationales.F03: Lesions with central ulceration and blackish crusting are concerning for a fungal infection.
rationales.F05: Immunocompromised status increases the risk of opportunistic infections, including Cryptococcosis.

rationales.F09: Histopathological examination shows a dermal collection of lymphocytes, histiocytes, and macrophages, which could be consistent with a fungal infection.
rationales.F10: Intracellular yeasts with surrounding halos are characteristic of Cryptococcosis.
